summary.text: Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms, looked at from molecules and cells up to organisms, populations, and ecosystems.
Five themes sit at its center: the cell, genes and heredity, evolution, energy transformation, and homeostasis.
Modern biology rests on evolution by natural selection and on the molecular understanding of genes encoded in DNA.

facts.label: Cell theory accepted
facts.value: By the 1860s most biologists accepted all three tenets

facts.label: Human Genome Project
facts.value: Launched in 1990 to map the human genome

items.prompt: A researcher asks how a living thing gets and uses fuel to keep going. Which central theme of biology is she working on?

options.label: Genes and heredity, passing on traits

items.explain: Energy transformation is the theme about sustaining life processes.

items.prompt: Your body keeps working in a steady way whether it is hot or cold outside. Which central theme of biology describes this?

options.label: Evolution as the driver of diversity
The cell as the basic unit of life

items.explain: Homeostasis is the maintenance of internal stability.

items.prompt: A scientist studies a whole forest and the plants and animals living together in it. At which level of organization is she working?
items.explain: Biology examines life from molecules and cells to organisms, populations, and ecosystems; a whole community living together is the ecosystem level.

items.prompt: A team deliberately tries a change and records its effect on living things. Which of biology's methods are they using?
items.explain: Biology's methods include observation, experimentation, and mathematical modeling; deliberately trying a change is experimentation.

items.prompt: Schleiden and Schwann said cells are the basic unit of organisms and each has the characteristics of life, yet they still backed spontaneous generation. Which tenet did Remak and Virchow establish?

options.label: Cells are the basic unit of every organism
Each cell has all the traits of living things
All cells come from the division of other cells
Living cells can arise from non-living matter

items.explain: Remak and Virchow established that all cells come from the division of other cells, which by the 1860s completed cell theory.

items.prompt: Mendel's work on inheritance was not appreciated until the early 20th century. What then made evolution a unified theory?

options.label: Reconciling Darwin's evolution with classical genetics
The discovery of the double helix structure of DNA
The cracking of the genetic code by Khorana and others
The launch of the Human Genome Project to map genes

items.explain: The modern synthesis reconciled Darwinian evolution with classical genetics.
